clinicalText.interpretation: Kidney function tests detect and monitor disease of the kidney. Higher blood levels of urea and creatinine indicate poorer kidney function. Creatinine is used as a marker of the severity of impairment — creatinine itself is not harmful, but a raised level indicates the kidneys are not clearing waste products properly. Dehydration can also raise urea independently of kidney disease. Kidney function is commonly checked before and during treatment with medicines that can occasionally damage the kidneys (nephrotoxic drugs). Correlate clinically.

tests.name: Prothrombin Time (PT/INR)
tests.printNote: INR = (Patient PT / Control PT) ^ ISI. Set your reagent lot’s ISI and mean normal control on this test — both are instrument/reagent specific. Reference ranges shown are standard adult values; confirm against your kit insert. INR 0.8–1.2 applies to a NON-anticoagulated patient — therapeutic targets differ (commonly 2.0–3.0 on warfarin, 2.5–3.5 for mechanical valves).

tests.printNote: AMH reflects OVARIAN RESERVE. Interpretation is AGE-DEPENDENT and must be read against the patient's age — a value that is unremarkable at 38 can be concerning at 25. LOW values suggest diminished ovarian reserve (the Bologna criteria reference 0.5-1.1 ng/mL as indicating diminished ovarian function; below about 0.4-0.5 ng/mL is regarded as severely low). HIGH values are most commonly associated with PCOS, where levels typically run 2-4 times higher than age-matched controls (roughly above 3.0-5.0 ng/mL). There is no universally established threshold for diminished ovarian reserve and results DIFFER BETWEEN ANALYSERS — each lab should confirm its own ranges against its kit insert before reporting a value as normal or abnormal. Conversion: 1 ng/mL = 7.14 pmol/L.

tests.name: Widal Test
tests.methodology: Widal slide agglutination (tube agglutination where confirmation is indicated)

parameters.name: TO (S. typhi O)
parameters.raisedNote: A raised O (somatic) titre suggests recent/active infection.

parameters.name: TH (S. typhi H)
parameters.raisedNote: A raised H (flagellar) titre may reflect current or past infection, or prior vaccination.

parameters.name: AH (S. paratyphi A H)
parameters.raisedNote: A raised AH titre points toward S. paratyphi A exposure.

parameters.name: BH (S. paratyphi B H)
parameters.raisedNote: A raised BH titre points toward S. paratyphi B exposure.

titerInterpretations.negative: All titres are below the significance threshold — serologically NEGATIVE for enteric fever. A single titre is only suggestive; if clinical suspicion persists, repeat after 7–10 days (a fourfold rise in paired sera is confirmatory).
titerInterpretations.positive: Raised titre for {antigens} — at or above the significance threshold, consistent with enteric fever in a compatible clinical setting.
titerInterpretations.borderline: Borderline titre for {antigens} — one dilution below this lab's significance threshold. CLINICAL CORRELATION IS REQUIRED: this may reflect past exposure, prior vaccination, or early infection. If enteric fever is suspected, repeat in 7–10 days — a fourfold rise in paired sera is what confirms it.

tests.printNote: LIMITATIONS OF A SINGLE WIDAL. (1) One titre has limited diagnostic value — the definitive pattern is a FOURFOLD RISE in paired sera drawn 7–10 days apart. (2) Raised H (flagellar) titres PERSIST for months to years after past infection or vaccination, so a raised TH alone is weak evidence of current illness. (3) FALSE POSITIVES occur through cross-reaction with malaria, dengue and other febrile illnesses, and in chronic liver disease. (4) Cutoffs are REGION-DEPENDENT: the defaults here follow published Indian baseline-titre studies (TO ≥1:80, TH ≥1:160), and a lab should ideally establish its own local baseline. AH/BH are contested between ≥1:80 and ≥1:160 — confirm against your own practice. Every cutoff is editable per parameter in the Test editor, and this note is editable too.

tests.name: High Sensitivity CRP
tests.printNote: Qualitative latex slide agglutination — Positive/Negative is the result. When positive, the highest dilution still agglutinating gives a semi-quantitative titre. Each lab establishes its own reference range.

tests.name: H. pylori Stool Antigen
tests.printNote: Detects H. pylori antigen in stool — indicates ACTIVE infection.

tests.name: RA Factor (Rheumatoid Arthritis)
tests.printNote: Qualitative latex slide agglutination — Positive/Negative is the result. When positive, the highest dilution still agglutinating gives a semi-quantitative titre (approximate concentration ≈ 8 IU/mL × titre). Each lab establishes its own reference range.

tests.name: C-Reactive Protein (CRP)
tests.printNote: Qualitative latex slide agglutination — Positive/Negative is the result. When positive, the highest dilution still agglutinating gives a semi-quantitative titre (approximate concentration ≈ 6 mg/L × titre). Each lab establishes its own reference range.

tests.name: H. pylori Antibody
tests.printNote: Detects H. pylori antibodies (IgG/IgM/IgA). Antibodies may persist after clearance, so a positive result does not necessarily indicate active infection — correlate clinically (stool antigen preferred for active infection).

tests.name: TORCH-4 IgM Profile (CLIA)
tests.printNote: IgM cutoffs are specific to the reagent lot and analyser — enter them from your kit insert (Tests → TORCH-4 → edit each parameter). Until a cutoff is set the value is reported without an interpretation. A positive IgM alone does not date an infection; in pregnancy confirm with paired sera and IgG avidity.

tests.name: Brucella Agglutination Test
tests.printNote: A single titre is only suggestive — a fourfold rise in paired sera is confirmatory. Antibodies may persist after past infection; correlate clinically.

titerInterpretations.negative: Both antigens are below the significance threshold — serologically NEGATIVE / non-reactive for Brucella.
titerInterpretations.positive: Raised titre for {antigens} — at or above the significance threshold, suggestive of brucellosis in a compatible clinical setting.

tests.name: Urine for Glucose
tests.printNote: Benedict's test read by colour: Blue = Nil · Green = Trace · Yellow-Green = 1+ · Yellow/Orange = 2+ · Orange-Red = 3+ · Brick Red = 4+.

tests.name: Urine Micro Protein (24 Hour)

validity.message: 24-hour protein not calculated — enter the measured 24-hour urine volume

tests.printNote: 24-hour protein is calculated from the spot concentration and the measured 24-hour volume: protein (mg/dL) × volume (mL) ÷ 100. Both must be entered for the total to be reported.
